content: Autoimmune type 1 diabetes represents approximately 5-10% of all diabetes cases. This condition arises due to the immune system's targeted destruction of pancreatic β-cells, which results in a deficiency of insulin production. Specific genetic factors, particularly certain HLA-DR and HLA-DQ haplotypes, are strongly linked to an increased susceptibility to developing type 1 diabetes. High-risk alleles include DRB10301 and DQB10201 (commonly referred to as DR3-DQ2) as well as DRB10401 and DQB10302 (known as DR4-DQ8). Testing for the presence of autoantibodies is a valuable tool for identifying individuals at risk, especially in those who have a family history of autoimmune diseases.
